newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia wants no more OSCE mediation in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Russia wants no more OSCE mediation in Chechnya.

text.p: Russia said on Friday that it no longer wanted the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE)'s mission in Chechnya to mediate between Moscow and the rebel region.

The OSCE said on Thursday it had appointed Danish diplomat Rudolf Thorning-Petersen to take over its mission in Chechnya from Tim Guldimann, who helped broker a deal to end 21 months of fighting between Russian troops and separatist fighters.

Guldimann, a Swiss diplomat, also played a key role in the organisation and monitoring of democratic elections in the breakaway republic in January and in efforts to find a permanent peace settlement building on last August's deal.
The Russian foreign ministry said in a statement on Friday that Thorning-Petersen should play a different role.

"The need for mediation by the OSCE representative has fallen away, since there is of course a direct dialogue between the central authorities and the new leadership of Chechnya as a part of the Russian Federation," the statement said.
Thorning-Petersen should concentrate instead on monitoring human rights, helping to establish democratic institutions, the return of refugees and humanitarian aid, it said.

The peace deal involved pulling out the troops in return for a postponement of a decision on Chechnya's political status -- the issue at the heart of the conflict in which tens of thousands of people, mostly civilians, were killed.

Chechnya is seeking formal independence but Moscow refuses any concession on sovereignty. Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov said on Wednesday that talks on a permanent political settlement had reached a dead end.

Maskhadov, who led the rebels' successful fight against Moscow before becoming president, said Chechnya faced a "political and economic blockade" and urged Russian President Boris Yeltsin to intervene personally to reach a peace deal.

Chechen officials were not immediately available for comment on the foreign ministry statement. Maskhadov's entourage have always strongly supported the OSCE's mediating role in Chechnya, seeing it as an added lever to their cause.
The foreign ministry statement said Moscow had informed OSCE of the change of emphasis for its representative at a meeting of the organisation's Permanent Council on March 13.
A spokesman at the Vienna-based OSCE declined to comment directly on the statement, which he said they had not seen.

But he said that apart from human rights, aid and refugee issues, Thorning-Petersen's official mandate said he should "promote peaceful resolution of the crisis and stabilisation of the situation" and "pursue dialogue and negotiations with a view to establishing a ceasefire".
The OSCE seeks to prevent conflicts and ease tensions while promoting democracy, arms control and human rights in Europe.
